text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The 1997/98 (July-June) budget due on June 13 will not offer any incentive or salary rise for government servants, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- The ruling Pakistan Muslim League has decided to join the coalition government in Balochistan province.
- Iran has halted the flow of most goods to Afghnaistan through its land border, traders say.
- Turkmenistan has called for regional efforts to persuade warring factions in Afghanistan to talk out their differences.
- The Pakistan People's Party candidate for an election was shot dead in Lahore.
- The murder of Murtaza Bhutto, brother of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, and seven of his party workers was an extra-judicial killing by police, a judicial inquiry said.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The state-run National Bank of Pakistan has offered to raise 15 billion rupees for the government through floatation of an exchangeable bond locally and abroad.
- Sugar mills have urged the government to allow import of raw sugar.
- The textile sector finally appears to be coming out of the trough after facing a recession of three years.
- The administrative expenditure of nationalised commercial banks is nearly four times higher than that of foreign banks.
FINANCIAL POST

- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the budget for 1997/98 (July-June) would augment revenue collection by reforming tax machinery, cut inflation to a single digit and boost exports to arrest the mounting budget deficit.
- Employees of banks and financial institutions will observe June 10 as a black day in protest against the government's decision to ban unions in banks.
THE NEWS
- The government requires an additional 40 billion rupees to bring down the deficit to five percent of gross domestic product in 1997/98 (July-June) from 6.2 percent in 1996/97.
THE MUSLIM
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto said her spouse Asif Ali Zardari had been exonerated by the findings of a judicial inquiry into the killing of her brother Murtaza Bhutto.
THE FRONTIER POST
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan said he would visit three Central Asian States including Turkmenistan from June 18 to 20 before his visit to Russia from July 7 to 8.
THE NATION
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has summoned his allies on June 12 to brief them on the 1997/98 (July-June) budget.
-- Islamabad newsroom 274757
